title: The omission construction must pass to the named elementary submodel.
details: Schlicht, An Introduction to Model Theory, PDF dated 2021-07-13, Theorem 4.1.6 proof, printed p.20, first chooses an arbitrary model M of the completed expanded theory, shows that the interpretations of the new constants form an elementary substructure, then says the type is omitted in M. The construction only ensures failure of a type formula at each tuple of named elements; unnamed elements of the ambient M need not fail the type. For example, expand the standard arithmetic structure by countably many constants naming every natural number, and take its complete expanded theory. Every named element fails the partial type consisting of inequalities from all numerals. Compactness nevertheless gives an elementary extension of that expanded structure with an unnamed element realizing all those inequalities. Repair: take the elementary submodel with carrier the named elements (or the corresponding Henkin term model), and then take its original-language reduct. Every tuple there is covered by the scheduled omission requirements. The theorem remains valid with this corrected last step. The corpus omission construction explicitly takes this named elementary submodel and separates its omission guarantee from the behavior of arbitrary ambient models. The earlier realization theorem does not use the faulty deduction.
